Two down. The next gap is in how the remaining failure messages get verified.

**Question:** How exactly should the error text be pinned down for the failure paths that currently have no specified wording — invalid username, short password, duplicate username, unknown account, bad usage, and unusable store? (FR-027)

**Why it matters:** The constitution requires every error path to have a test asserting the message content, and right now six of them say only "reports the problem on standard error" — so there is nothing for a test to assert against.

**Recommended:** Option A — give each failure path one exact string, the way `ok`, `invalid credentials`, `account locked` and `registered USERNAME` already are. It leaves no wording undecided, every test is a plain equality check, and it extends the discipline SC-002 already applies to the four known messages.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Specify one exact message string per failure path; tests assert full equality |
| B | Specify a required substring per path (e.g. must contain `no such account`); wording otherwise free |
| C | Leave wording to the implementation; tests assert only non-empty stderr plus the exit status |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
